topicTitle: Isomerism in organic compounds: definition and classification of isomerism; structural isomerism and its types
notes: **Isomerism:** same molecular formula but different structural arrangement gives different compounds with different properties.
**Structural isomerism:** same molecular formula, different connectivity of atoms.
**Chain isomerism:** different carbon skeleton. Example: $C_4H_{10}$ gives n-butane (straight) and isobutane (branched).
**Position isomerism:** same carbon skeleton, functional group at different position. Example: propan-1-ol vs propan-2-ol.
**Functional isomerism:** same molecular formula, different functional groups. Example: ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$, alcohol) vs dimethyl ether ($CH_3OCH_3$, ether).
**Metamerism:** different alkyl groups on either side of a functional group in compounds with same general formula. Example: diethyl ether ($C_2H_5OC_2H_5$) vs methyl propyl ether ($CH_3OC_3H_7$).
**Tautomerism:** dynamic equilibrium between two isomers differing in position of a proton and a double bond. Example: keto-enol tautomerism of acetone.
